- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., price drops sharply after peak), model often fails to correct; anticipate and slightly lower forecast in next 7–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% in the 10–15 day window.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before adjustment.
